experiment: v22 versus v23 name-and-tag interpretation comparison
approval: User approved testing the proposed v23 prompt. Repeat the preceding comparison design: three fresh trials per version on the same three groups, 18 calls total.
plane_update: No Plane tool exposed; no external update performed.
question: Does the added name/tag interpretation instruction reduce unsupported commercial-chain titles while preserving the two control subjects?
hypotheses: The new rule may prevent treating a name's words as a literal description.
The model may treat the disputed interpretation as established meaning, in which case the rule may not help.
execution: One fresh wrapper config/process/thread and empty workspace per call. First call alone, then maximum three concurrent calls. Alternate versions and rotate group order. No automatic retries.
review: Read every title beside the exact masks. Judge meaning, not an exact preferred title. Preserve ordinary background knowledge and accepted broad interpretations; count unsupported commercial chains as the target error. Record ambiguity separately. No reviewer hints enter generation.
limits: Three reused groups, not a general holdout. Coffeechain and coffee preparation share one underlying note through different masks. These outputs cannot establish the model's internal mechanism.
frozen: No prompt, mask, input order or wrapper changes during the experiment. No saved-title replacement, freeze, TRUE run or hierarchy changes.
budget: Existing authorized Codex subscription only. No API billing, purchase, rental or account switch.
